# Domain schema api/v0

Public API declarations: declaration entities carry `data.signature`, and optionally `data.contract`, their compatibility facts in terms every ecosystem shares. The schema is published at its ID, `https://schemas.projections.githubnext.com/api/v0.json`; it is generated from TypeBox
definitions into [`packages/schemas/schemas/api/v0.json`](../../../packages/schemas/schemas/api/v0.json).

An extraction in this schema is an [extraction](extraction.md) whose `schema` is `api/v0`; the extraction schema applies this one
to it.

## Typed data

The engine checks every typed field, and reports a violation at its path. Other `data` fields are open JSON.

### Entities

| Kind | Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `export`, `type`, `member`, `function`, `class`, `interface`, `method`, `property`, `enum` | `data.signature` | string | Yes | The declaration as source shows it, such as `(a: string) => void`. |
| Every kind | `data.contract` | [`contract`](#contract) |  | The facts compatibility rules read about the declaration, in terms every ecosystem shares. |

## Definitions

### `constituent`

One member of a union type.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | Yes | The constituent as the language writes it, such as `"low"`. |
| `primitive` | string |  | The primitive it is, or a literal of it widens to, such as `string` or `undefined`; absent for other types. |

No other properties are allowed.

### `typeRef`

A type where values flow: its text as the language writes it, and, when the extractor resolves it, its union constituents.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | Yes | The type as the language writes it, such as `System.Int32` or `number \| undefined`. |
| `union` | array of [`constituent`](#constituent) |  | Each constituent of the type, a single one when it is no union; absent when the extractor resolves no unions. |

No other properties are allowed.

### `access`

A property's accessors, each with who can use it; an accessor that is absent doesn't exist.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `read` | `"public"` or `"protected"` |  | The getter. |
| `write` | `"public"` or `"protected"` |  | The setter. |
| `init` | `"public"` or `"protected"` |  | An accessor that sets it only while an instance is created: .NET `init`. |

No other properties are allowed.

### `parameter`

A parameter, in position order.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | Yes | The parameter's name. |
| `type` | [`typeRef`](#typeref) | Yes | The parameter's type. |
| `optional` | boolean | Yes | Callers may omit it. |
| `variadic` | boolean | Yes | It takes any number of arguments: a TypeScript rest parameter, a .NET `params` array. |
| `default` | string |  | The value an omitted argument takes, as the language writes it. |
| `passing` | `"value"` or `"ref"` or `"out"` or `"in"` or `"ref readonly"` | Yes | How the argument is passed: by `value`, or by reference as .NET `ref`, `out`, `in` and `ref readonly`. |
| `attributes` | array of string |  | The parameter's attributes, as the language writes them. |

No other properties are allowed.

### `typeParameter`

A generic parameter.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | Yes | The parameter's name, such as `T` or Rust's lifetime `'a`. |
| `constraints` | array of string | Yes | What an argument must satisfy, each as the language writes it: bounds, constraints or a single constraint type. |
| `default` | string |  | The argument used when none is given. |
| `type` | string |  | A value parameter's type, such as a Rust `const` generic's `usize`. |

No other properties are allowed.

### `signature`

One way to call or construct a declaration.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `parameters` | array of [`parameter`](#parameter) | Yes | Its parameters, in order. |
| `returns` | [`typeRef`](#typeref) | Yes | What a call returns; a constructor its instance, or the language's void. |
| `returnAttributes` | array of string |  | Attributes of what it returns, as the language writes them. |
| `typeParameters` | array of [`typeParameter`](#typeparameter) |  | Its generic parameters. |

No other properties are allowed.

### `supertype`

A type a declaration derives from or implements.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `relation` | `"extends"` or `"implements"` | Yes | Whether it derives from the type (a base class, a supertrait, an interface an interface extends) or implements it. |
| `type` | string | Yes | The type, as the language writes it. |

No other properties are allowed.

### `contract`

The language-neutral facts compatibility rules read about one declaration. Booleans that are absent are false. Facts only one ecosystem's rules read are in `native`.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `declaration` | `"package"` or `"module"` or `"class"` or `"struct"` or `"union"` or `"enum"` or `"interface"` or `"alias"` or `"type"` or `"function"` or `"method"` or `"constructor"` or `"property"` or `"field"` or `"variant"` or `"constant"` or `"variable"` or `"event"` or `"index"` or `"call"` or `"construct"` or `"associated-type"` or `"implementation"` or `"re-export"` or `"macro"` | Yes | What kind of declaration it is. |
| `term` | [`text`](extraction.md#text) | Yes | The ecosystem's own word for the kind of declaration, such as Rust's `trait-method`, Go's `func` or .NET's `record class`; a change of `term` is a change of kind. |
| `visibility` | `"public"` or `"protected"` | Yes | Who can use it. |
| `static` | boolean |  | It belongs to its type rather than to instances. |
| `abstract` | boolean |  | It has no implementation: implementers or subclasses must provide it (.NET `abstract` members and interface members without a default body, TypeScript's `abstract`, Rust trait items without a default, Go interface methods); a class that is abstract can't be instantiated. |
| `sealed` | boolean |  | Consumers can't inherit or implement it: a .NET type that is sealed, static or has no accessible constructor; a Rust trait with a supertrait outside the public API; a Go interface with unexported methods. |
| `readonly` | boolean |  | Consumers can read it but not assign it: .NET `readonly` fields, TypeScript `readonly` properties, Rust statics that aren't `mut`. |
| `required` | boolean |  | Code creating an instance must set it: .NET `required` members. |
| `optional` | boolean |  | It may be absent: a TypeScript optional (`?`) member. |
| `nonExhaustive` | boolean |  | It may gain members without a breaking change, so consumers may not match every variant or name every field in literals and patterns: Rust `#[non_exhaustive]`. |
| `hiddenMembers` | boolean |  | It has fields or variants consumers can't see, so they can't construct it from its fields or destructure it exhaustively: Rust private fields and hidden variants. |
| `type` | [`typeRef`](#typeref) |  | Its type: a field's, property's, variable's, constant's or event's; the type an alias names; the type an implementation is for; a Go function's or method's type. |
| `value` | string |  | A constant's or enum member's value, as the language writes it. |
| `underlying` | string |  | The type an enum or a defined type is represented by: a .NET enum's, a Go defined type's. |
| `source` | string |  | What a re-export re-exports, as a path. |
| `access` | [`access`](#access) |  | A property's accessors. |
| `attributes` | array of string |  | Its attributes or annotations, each as the language writes it, such as .NET `System.ObsoleteAttribute("Use Run")`. |
| `signatures` | array of [`signature`](#signature) |  | How it is called or constructed: one signature, or each overload in order. An indexer has one, whose parameters are its keys. |
| `typeParameters` | array of [`typeParameter`](#typeparameter) |  | Its generic parameters; a callable's are its signatures'. |
| `supertypes` | array of [`supertype`](#supertype) |  | What it derives from or implements, as its ecosystem lists them: .NET base types and every implemented interface, TypeScript heritage clauses, Rust supertraits and the trait an implementation implements, the Go interfaces of the package a type implements. |
| `constraints` | array of string |  | What an associated type must satisfy, each as the language writes it. |
| `native` | object |  | Ecosystem-specific facts, read only by that ecosystem's compatibility rules. Each public API extractor documents its own. |

No other properties are allowed.
